messages:
incident-bot: Paging oncall: high-rate GPU host resets observed in us-west-2 cluster (autoscale-group inference-prod-usw2-1). Severity: P1. Please acknowledge.

alice (oncall): Acked. I'm on it. Any immediate customer impact visible?

simon (support): Seeing a spike in 503s for /v1/generate, about 18% errors over last 6m. Several long-tail client retries. I'll surface to customers if this persists.

carla (sre): Correlating logs — host-level kernel logs show repeated NV_HOST_ERR messages and `Xid` entries. Likely GPU driver resets.

ben (infra): I'm pulling node list: 9 hosts flagged by Wavefront with kernel reset events. Marking them in the infra dashboard. Will snapshot instance metadata.

alice (oncall): Plan: cordon+drain the most noisy hosts, failover traffic to adjacent AZs / dedicated pool. Need runtime to confirm can tolerate de-scheduling.


 dave (runtime): We see container restarts tied to node-level driver resets. Runtime picks up OOM/cgroup restarts after NV reset. We can scale up the spare pool and shift traffic. Triggering a canary shift now: `routes.set-weight model-inference v2=0.0, v1=100` to reduce load on affected model instances.

emily (eng-oncall): Initiating drain on node inference-usw2-37. Command: `kubectl cordon node/inference-usw2-37 && kubectl drain node/inference-usw2-37 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

ben (infra): Noted some nodes are flapping during drain. Drain hangs because kubelet loses contact after driver reset. I'm going to forcibly evict pods via `--force` if necessary.

carla (sre): Adding diagnostic checklist for each affected host: `dmesg | grep -i nvrm || true`, `journalctl -k -u kubelet --since "10m"`, `nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS,ECC,DRIVER`. Post outputs here.

alice (oncall): Can someone paste a sample kernel/Xid snippet? Need concrete error codes to triage.

ben (infra): Paste from inference-usw2-41:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid=9876, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1234.568012] kernel: NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 1234.570000] nvidia-modeset: GPU crtc dissociate
```

carla (sre): ECC counters on that host: `Single-bit ECC errors: 1843; Double-bit ECC errors: 0` — single-bit ramping. Could indicate a noisy DIMM or thermal issue causing corrections and ultimately driver instability.

alice (oncall): This is different from previous pure Xid bursts — single-bit ECC climb then Xid 79 resets. Also timeline matches a firmware update we rolled last week? Ben, any nodes with recent BIOS/firmware changes?

ben (infra): Checking. A subset had a vendor microcode update applied 36h ago. Flagging them. Also, these nodes are all on driver 535.54.03.

vendor-esc: Vendor escalation ticket created: E-92817. Provided logs and `nvidia-bug-report.sh` archives. Asked for recommended driver/firmware action.

alice (oncall): Short-term mitigations: 1) Move traffic off affected AZ, 2) cordon/drain noisy nodes, 3) scale up healthy capacity in other pools, 4) enable model fallback to smaller quantized variants where possible to reduce GPU memory pressure.


 dave (runtime): Implemented fallback routing for large-gen models: `split-traffic --from inference-prod --to inference-fallback --pct 30` to reduce memory pressure. Also lowered max batch size for canary to reduce KV cache pressure.

simon (support): Customers A and B reported elevated latencies; notified them we're investigating and performing mitigation. Drafting status message: "We’re seeing transient GPU host instability; routing and capacity changes underway; no data loss reported."

carla (sre): From `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC` on another host:
```
ECC Error Counts
  Volatile
    Single-bit: 271
    Double-bit: 0
  Aggregate
    Single-bit: 12349
    Double-bit: 2
```
Double-bit aggregated low but single-bit count accumulation is accelerating on several hosts. That is suspicious.

alice (oncall): Ben, please isolate nodes with high single-bit rates from fleet scheduling and create a quarantine label so autoscaler won't put workloads there.

ben (infra): Done. Added label `gpu=quarantine` and updated ASG scaling policy to avoid those instances.

vendor-esc: Quick note from vendor: Xid 79 often follows hardware link flaps; they asked for PCIe topology and logs. Suggested testing with driver 535.86.08 as a quick experiment.

alice (oncall): We should not mass-upgrade drivers mid-incident. Proposed: pick 1 quarantined host, repro/do stress test after upgrade, verify stability for 30m, then consider wider roll. Who can run the smoke test?

ben (infra): I'll take one node (inference-usw2-49), snapshot and run driver upgrade to 535.86.08 in isolated host, and run `stress-ng --matrix` + synthetic inference load. ETA 18m.

carla (sre): Also run memtest and `mcelog` checks; if ECC counters reduce after power cycle that hints at transient thermal/unclean seating. If they persist, escalate hardware replacement.

emily (eng-oncall): Noted a pattern: nodes with high single-bit counts are all from the same procurement lot. Could be a batch DIMM issue. I'll coordinate with hardware ops if vendor confirms.

simon (support): Sending proactive update to affected customers with ETA ~45m and note about degraded error rates and routing changes.

alice (oncall): Any sign of degraded model quality or token corruption? Dave?

 dave (runtime): No evidence of token corruption. Reqs either succeed slower or return 503s. No incorrect outputs detected. Good sign — likely infra-only.

ben (infra): Upgrade started on inference-usw2-49. Will post driver install log and `nvidia-smi` after reboot.


deploy-bot: Deployment event: new routing weights applied by alice at 2149001425.

ben (infra): Post-upgrade `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv` shows 535.86.08. Running synthetic load.

carla (sre): Observing that on upgraded host ECC Single-bit counts are steady (no further ramp) and no Xid 79 in last 12m. Good sign.

vendor-esc: Vendor says candidate driver looks stable on that hardware in their lab. Suggesting slow rollout to additional quarantined hosts. Also recommended firmware rollbacks to previous microcode on a test host if instability persists.

alice (oncall): Okay, plan: slow driver roll to remaining quarantined hosts in batches of 2, each with 30m verification. Meanwhile maintain routing split and keep quarantined label. Ben, coordinate with maint windows.

ben (infra): Will schedule batches. Next pair upgrading now (inference-usw2-37, inference-usw2-41).

simon (support): Updating customers: "We have implemented routing adjustments and are rolling a validated driver to affected hosts in batches. We'll continue monitoring; next customer update in 30 minutes." :thumbsup:

carla (sre): Action item list: 1) Confirm driver rollback/upgrade plan, 2) run hardware diagnostics on quarantined hosts, 3) ensure autoscaler excludes quarantined label, 4) create follow-up hardware replacement tickets for any node with persistent ECC growth. Assign owners.

alice (oncall): Owners: Ben infra (1,3), Carla SRE (2,4), Dave runtime (fallbacks and routing), Simon support (customer comms). I'll run incident timeline and handoff to night oncall at 2149001800 unless situation de-escalates.

emily (eng-oncall): I'll be reachable for any runtime regressions. If vendor suggests firmware change, escalate to PM for procurement window.

vendor-esc: Keep logs and bug reports attached to E-92817. Open to live debug call if needed.

alice (oncall): Handoff: Situation currently stabilizing after targeted driver test. Active work: batch driver rollout and hardware diagnostics. Severity remains P1 until all quarantined hosts pass verification or are replaced. Night oncall please watch wavefront alerts for `GPU Xid` > 10/min and `ECC Single-bit delta` > 500 within 30m.

carla (sre): I'll post a short postmortem template after we close incident with initial hypotheses and next steps.

simon (support): Final note for thread: customers A/B/C notified, no data loss, degraded latency and retries.

alice (oncall): Thanks team. Passing to night: emily (eng-oncall) as primary, carla backup. I'll paste incident channel link in handoff doc.

emily (eng-oncall): Ack — will monitor.

incident-bot: Incident update recorded: incident_id=inc-2149-01, status=mitigating, owners=[ben,carla,dave,simon], sla_impact=partial.

alice (oncall): Closing active coordination thread for now. Follow-ups in #postmortems.
